title: End-to-End Scenario
subtitle: Follow one call from Alice to Bob through number discovery, caller verification, encryption and direct routing, step by step.
endNote: Every PSTN2 capability, working together on a single call.

segments.text: Alice is a customer of Alpha Telecom, a large mobile carrier.
Bob is a customer of Bravo Networks, a regional fixed-line provider.
Alice wants to call Bob, and both providers have deployed PSTN2.
Let’s follow the call, step by step, in real time.
Alice dials Bob’s number on her mobile.
Her phone sends a SIP INVITE into Alpha’s network, and Alpha receives the call request.
segments.say: Her phone sends a sip invite into Alpha’s network, and Alpha receives the call request.

segments.text: Elapsed time: fifty milliseconds.
Now the PSTN2 steps begin, in the background.
First, Alpha must find out which provider serves Bob’s number today. Its cache has no entry.
Alpha’s copy of Ofcom’s numbering list names the Range Holder, Charlie Comms, and gives its PSTN2 address.
Alpha asks Charlie. Bob ported his number away, so Charlie redirects Alpha to Bravo Networks.
Alpha asks Bravo, and Bravo answers: held, signed with its key. Alpha caches the answer.
Elapsed time: about a hundred milliseconds. Alpha now knows where to send the call.
Alpha sends Bravo a signed request to take the call directly, with Alice’s number as the caller ID.
Before accepting, Bravo checks the caller. It finds Alice’s provider with the same discovery, and asks Alpha: did you originate this call?
Alpha checks its live call record and answers: yes, verified. The answer is signed with Alpha’s key.
The call is proven genuine, not spoofed. Elapsed time: a hundred and fifty milliseconds.
Alpha’s request and Bravo’s answer each carry the provider’s identity key, and the encryption it supports.
They agree on SRTP, with AES-256.
segments.say: They agree on S R T P, with A E S two fifty-six.

segments.text: Fresh keys, for this call only, come from a DTLS 1.3 handshake. Each side’s identity key proves who is at the other end.
segments.say: Fresh keys, for this call only, come from a D T L S one point three handshake. Each side’s identity key proves who is at the other end.

segments.text: All media will be encrypted end to end. Elapsed time: two hundred and fifty milliseconds.
Bravo’s answer also gives the address and port for the media, so the call can go direct.
No transit providers in between.
They agree on the Opus codec, for high-quality voice.
The media path is ready at four hundred milliseconds. Now Bob’s phone can ring.
Alpha’s verification answer also carries Alice’s caller details.
Her chosen display name, verified by Alpha, and an optional business logo.
Bravo shows this on Bob’s screen. Bob sees far more than a number.
Bob sees that Alice is verified, and answers.
The encrypted media path comes alive. Alice’s voice travels directly from Alpha to Bravo, with no intermediaries.
Encryption keeps it private. The direct path keeps it clear.
Under half a second of setup, then ringing: about 3.2 seconds from dialling to talking.
segments.say: Under half a second of setup, then ringing: about three point two seconds from dialling to talking.

segments.text: During the call, Alice and Bob enjoy HD audio.
segments.say: During the call, Alice and Bob enjoy H D audio.

segments.text: The Opus codec gives natural-sounding, wideband voice.
Direct routing keeps latency low, at around 40 milliseconds.
With fewer hops, there is less jitter and packet loss. The conversation is crystal clear.
Now imagine Alice needs to call 999. Alpha recognises the emergency number at once.
Alpha has her phone’s real-time location: GPS, the serving cell and nearby Wi-Fi.
The emergency call centre asks Alpha for it with a PSTN2 location query, and gets it immediately.
Not from yesterday’s batch file. Right now.
When Bravo answered held, Alpha cached the answer against Bob’s number, for 24 hours.
So next time anyone at Alpha calls Bob, Alpha skips the list and the Range Holder, and goes straight to Bravo. One query.
If Bob ever moves again, Bravo will answer: not held, invalidate your cache. Alpha simply discovers again, and the call still connects.
The network learns, call by call, with no central database.
Let’s compare. On today’s network, nobody can be sure a caller ID is genuine. With PSTN2, the caller is verified.
Today, calls cross several transit hops, unencrypted. PSTN2 connects directly, encrypted end to end.
Today’s voice quality is basic, and emergency location can be a day old. PSTN2 brings HD voice and real-time location.
segments.say: Today’s voice quality is basic, and emergency location can be a day old. P S T N two brings H D voice and real-time location.

segments.text: And call setup falls from five to eight seconds, to under one second.
A traditional call might cost around 5p a minute, much of it in transit fees.
segments.say: A traditional call might cost around five pence a minute, much of it in transit fees.

segments.text: With PSTN2 direct routing, it could be less than 1p a minute.
segments.say: With P S T N two direct routing, it could be less than a penny a minute.

segments.text: Across millions of calls, that adds up to millions of pounds.
Savings that can be passed on to customers, or invested in better networks.
To Alice and Bob, none of this complexity is visible.
Alice dials. Bob answers. They talk.
It just works, only better: clearer audio, faster setup, more trust and better privacy.
That is the promise of PSTN2: better technology, with a seamless experience.
This one call shows PSTN2’s capabilities working together.
Number discovery, caller verification, direct routing, encryption, branding and emergency location.
Not separate add-ons, but one integrated set of capabilities.
And every part of it can be built today, at the edge of the network, with no central database.
